dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: هَلَا بِيك. عِندِي شِقَّة حِلوَة گَرِيبَة مِن الجَامِع
dialogue.transliteration: hala biik. 3indi shigga 7ilwa greeba min ij-jaami3
dialogue.english: Welcome. I have a nice flat near the masjid.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: الشِّقَّة كُلَّش زِينَة
dialogue.transliteration: ish-shigga kullish zeena
dialogue.english: The flat is very nice.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام. تِدفَع إِيجَار شَهَر عَربُون، وِتِنتِگِل أَوَّل الشَّهَر
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. tidfa3 eejaar shahar 3arboon, w tintigil awwal ish-shahar
dialogue.english: Fine. You pay one month's rent as a deposit and move in at the start of the month.

pair.english: How much is the monthly rent?

response.english: Four hundred thousand dinars a month.

pair.english: How many bedrooms does it have?

response.english: From the first of the month.

lessons.culture: In Iraqi cities rent is quoted per month in dinars, and a flat is described by its rooms. The owner is called "صاحب الملك", and it is wise to ask what the rent covers, for example whether the neighbourhood generator (المولدة) is included, and to sign a written عقد before paying.

exercises.prompt: A man asks: "شكد الإيجار بالشهر؟" Say: four hundred thousand dinars a month.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللهُ، كُلَّش وَاسعَة
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a Allaah, kullish waas3a
dialogue.english: As Allah willed, it is very spacious.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: ما مُشكِلَة، وِبِيها دُولاب هُدُوم
dialogue.transliteration: ma mushkila, w biiha doolaab hdoom
dialogue.english: No problem, and it has a clothes wardrobe.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: بَس لَمبَة المَمَرّ ما تِشتَغِل
dialogue.transliteration: bass lamba il-mamarr ma tishtighil
dialogue.english: But the corridor light bulb does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: ما عَلَيك، صَلِّحهَا لَو سَمَحِت وآنِي آخُذ الشِّقَّة
dialogue.transliteration: ma 3aleek, Salli7ha law sama7it w aani aakhudh ish-shigga
dialogue.english: No problem, please fix it and I will take the flat.

pair.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?
Where do I put the fridge?

lessons.culture: A flat is described by its rooms: the guest room (غرفة الضيوف), the bedrooms, the kitchen and the bathrooms. Many Iraqi homes keep a room for receiving guests. A flat may be rented furnished or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners, which matter in the summer heat.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "المكيف يشتغل؟" Say: yes, it works well.

too_formal.feedback: This is written Arabic; Iraqis say "يشتغل زين".

exercises.tip: "غرفة الضيوف" is the room for guests.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حَاضِر. وِالبَاب هَم ما يِنسَدّ زِين
dialogue.transliteration: 7aaDir. wil-baab hamm ma yinsadd zeen
dialogue.english: Right away. And the door does not close well either.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: رَاح أَشُوفَه بَعَد شْوَيَّة. بَدِّل اللَّمبَة أَوَّل
dialogue.transliteration: raa7 ashoofa ba3ad shwayya. baddil il-lamba awwal
dialogue.english: I will look at it in a little while. Change the bulb first.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: خَلَّصِت. جَرِّب الحَنَفِيَّة
dialogue.transliteration: khallaSit. jarrib il-7anafiyya
dialogue.english: I have finished. Try the tap.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا
dialogue.transliteration: jazaaka Allaahu khayran
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.

lessons.culture: A small repair is often a favour between brothers, relatives and neighbours before anyone is paid, and the helper is thanked with "جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا". People say "الحمد لله" when a job ends well and "إن شاء الله" when they promise to try. For a bigger problem you call the سبّاك (plumber) or the كهربائي (electrician), and it is polite to ask the price before the work starts.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "تگدر تصلّحه؟" Say: yes, I will try.

too_formal.feedback: This is written Arabic; Iraqis use "راح" for the future.

exercises.tip: "راح" before a verb makes the future.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "شكراً، هسّه يشتغل". Answer: Praise be to Allah.
exercises.tip: This is fixed Islamic wording, shared by all dialects, so it is not changed for Iraqi.

pair.english: Will you receive our mail while we travel?

lessons.culture: In Islam a neighbour has a great right, and Iraqi neighbours share food, visit one another when ill and keep an eye on each other's homes while they travel. Sending a dish to the family that has just moved in is a common way to start a friendship, and tea (چاي) is offered to every guest.

exercises.prompt: Your new neighbours say: "احنا جيرانكم الجداد". Welcome them.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct and polite; in daily speech Iraqis often say "هلا بيكم".

exercises.tip: To one man: "هلا بيك"; to one woman: "هلا بيچ".

exercises.tip: "راح" plus a verb makes the future.

challenge.title: Viewing a Flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 8 lines where you ask about a flat for rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say what you will take. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 18.
required_elements: A question about the rent or the number of bedrooms using شكد or چم.
A question about the floor, the lift, or whether water and electricity are included.
A request to see the flat using أگدر.
A question about the kitchen or the furniture using وين or مفروشة.
A closing decision with آخذها or أريد عقد إيجار.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. آنِي أَدَوِّر شِقَّة لِلإِيجَار. شَكَد الإِيجَار بِالشَّهَر؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. aani adawwir shigga lil-eejaar. shgadd il-eejaar bish-shahar?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. أَربَعمِيَّة أَلِف دِينَار بِالشَّهَر، وِبِيها ثَلَاث غُرَف نَوم
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. arba3miyya alif deenaar bish-shahar, w biiha thalaath ghuraf noom
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Four hundred thousand dinars a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: بِأَي طَابِگ؟ واكُو مَصعَد بِالعِمَارَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: b-ay Taabig? w aku maS3ad bil-3imaara?
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift in the building?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: بِالطَّابِگ الثَّانِي، وإِي اكُو مَصعَد. بَس الكَهرَبَا وِالمَاي مُو شَامْلِين
dialogue.transliteration: biT-Taabig ith-thaani, w ee aku maS3ad. bass il-kahraba wil-maay mu shaamliin
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and yes there is a lift. But electricity and water are not included.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أَگدَر أَشُوف الشِّقَّة هَسَّه؟ وِهيَّ مَفرُوشَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: agdar ashoof ish-shigga hassa? w hiyya mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat now? And is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّل. بِيها أَثَاث كَامِل، وِالمَطبَخ جَنِب غُرفَة الضُّيُوف
dialogue.transliteration: tfaDDal. biiha athaath kaamil, w il-maTbakh janib ghurfat iD-Dyoof
dialogue.english: Please come in. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: كُلَّش حِلوَة. رَاح آخُذها، وِأَرِيد عَقِد إِيجَار لِسَنَة
dialogue.transliteration: kullish 7ilwa. raa7 aakhudha, w areed 3agid eejaar li-sana
dialogue.english: Very nice. I will take it, and I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَمَام. تِدفَع إِيجَار شَهَر عَربُون
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. tidfa3 eejaar shahar 3arboon
dialogue.english: Fine. You pay one month's rent as a deposit.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا
dialogue.transliteration: jazaaka Allaahu khayran
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.
